prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The 2019 Conservative manifesto is a one‑nation plan to get Brexit done and unleash Britain’s potential by pairing superb public services with a dynamic, free‑enterprise economy—delivering security, opportunity and fairness across the whole United Kingdom.

Core promise: With a Conservative majority, Parliament will pass the signed, “oven‑ready” Brexit deal, take the UK out of the EU in January, end free movement, keep us out of the single market and customs union, and negotiate a friendly, zero‑alignment free trade agreement with the EU by December 2020—without extending the implementation period. Brexit will restore control of laws, borders, money and trade, while upholding high standards and strengthening the Union.

Public services and cost of living: Record NHS investment enshrined in law; 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 50 million extra GP appointments; 40 new hospitals and 20 upgrades; an NHS Visa; mental health on a par with physical health; no NHS in trade talks. Social care: £1bn extra every year, a cross‑party long‑term solution, and a guarantee no one will have to sell their home to pay for care. A tax guarantee: no rises in the rates of income tax, VAT or National Insurance; raise the NI threshold immediately, with the long‑term aim that the first £12,500 you earn is tax‑free. Protect pensioner benefits and the triple lock.

Law and order: 20,000 more police; tougher sentencing for serious offenders; end halfway release for the worst crimes; new powers against knife crime; more prison places; a Police Covenant in law; a national cyber force; stronger action on organised crime and victim support.

Immigration: An Australian‑style points system that prioritises skills and contribution, treats EU and non‑EU citizens equally, reduces low‑skilled migration, requires NHS contributions and five years’ residence before most benefits, and welcomes the best talent with bespoke visas.

Levelling up and infrastructure: A transport revolution (Northern Powerhouse Rail, Midlands Rail Hub), £100bn in responsible investment, gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025, restored Beeching lines, superbus networks, contactless ticketing, a massive pothole programme, and a new Towns Fund for safer, thriving high streets. Devolution across England and a UK Shared Prosperity Fund to bind the Union.

Housing: Build at least a million more homes in the Parliament, moving towards 300,000 a year; long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages to cut deposits; protect the Green Belt; infrastructure first; end “no‑fault” evictions; a lifetime tenant deposit; renewed Affordable Homes Programme; stamp duty surcharge for non‑resident buyers; empower social housing tenants.

Education and skills: £14bn extra for schools, higher teacher starting pay, strong discipline and standards, arts and sport investment, more SEND support, and a £3bn National Skills Fund; more apprenticeships tied to major projects; 20 Institutes of Technology; world‑class universities with fairer student finance.

Enterprise and trade: Back small businesses with business rates reform, late‑payment crackdowns, start‑up loans and procurement access; smarter regulation post‑Brexit; more R&D (towards 2.4% of GDP), a new high‑risk research agency, stronger life sciences; 10 freeports; 80% of UK trade covered by FTAs in three years (US, Australia, New Zealand, Japan), with high standards protected and the NHS off the table.

Environment, farming and fishing: Net Zero by 2050 via clean energy, offshore wind (40GW), EV infrastructure, carbon capture, energy efficiency, and a moratorium on fracking; a powerful Environment Bill, tree planting, plastics crackdown and recycling reform. Replace CAP with “public money for public goods” and leave the CFP, taking back control of UK waters with sustainable fishing.

Union, democracy and defence: Strengthen devolution, oppose a second Scottish referendum, safeguard Northern Ireland’s place in the UK internal market. Protect democracy with voter ID, fair boundaries and free speech; a Constitution, Democracy & Rights Commission. Exceed NATO 2%, modernise the Armed Forces, maintain Trident, boost cyber and Space Command, and support veterans.

The choice: A Conservative majority to deliver Brexit, stability and opportunity—or a Corbyn/Sturgeon coalition bringing more delay, higher taxes and two divisive referendums. Vote Conservative to get Brexit done and take Britain forward.
